solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One standing to split Democrats miles apart

indicators.note: the pair of Democrats is split apart so the other pieces sit between them

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat, and two of them give D and D
one is the Roman numeral I
a stance is a way of standing, or a position taken

explanation.surface: A lone figure taking a position that splits the Democratic party into two widely separated camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kept at a remove, with miles between them and others, has been put at a distance; past participle as adjective.

clue.text: Drinker gets into water, nothing more

indicators.note: more means something further is added after the first piece

parts.note: someone who takes a quick swim dips
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A boozer only ever gets into the water and does nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipso is informal slang, a clipped form of dipsomaniac, for an alcoholic or heavy drinker.

clue.text: Soft furnishings The Curtain Co's arranged on board

indicators.note: on board a ship means within it, so the shuffled letters go inside the ship

parts.note: board here stands for a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship

indicators.note: the letters of the firm's name are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A curtain company has laid out its soft furnishings on a board, perhaps a shop display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles the firm's name; 'on' with 'board' means aboard a ship, the usual steamship abbreviation going round the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small decorative cushions strewn over sofas and beds are a classic item of soft furnishing.

clue.text: What's central to teaching, always, for high flyer

indicators.note: the letters sitting in the centre of the word teaching are taken out

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A school motto: what always matters most in teaching is producing top performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A high flyer is a person of great success, someone who reaches high goals.

clue.text: South of cape, choice of routes for ill-starred traveller

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so this piece follows the cape

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
a choice between two routes: A ST (a street) or A WAY

explanation.surface: A traveller rounding a cape has a choice of routes and picks the unlucky one.
explanation.walkthrough: The routes are 'a street' (A ST) and 'a way' (A WAY), set side by side as the options on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwrecked sailor marooned on a desert island is the classic unlucky voyager, like Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: One stabs gang leader twice in overturned study

indicators.note: in places the doubled letter inside the turned-round study
in a down clue overturned means the word for study is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: twice means the chosen letter appears two times
the leader of gang is its first letter

explanation.surface: A violent tale: someone stabs a gang boss twice in a study that has been turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reads the verb for study upwards in this down clue; 'twice' doubles the gang's leader before 'in' tucks it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pointed blade is a weapon that stabs, so it can be described as one stabbing.

clue.text: Really like the French poodle, say

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a young poodle, like any young dog, is a pup

explanation.surface: Someone is very fond of the French poodle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the poodle as one example of a dog, here a young one.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoy something eagerly is to drink it in, the idiom from a dog lapping milk.

clue.text: Close to industrial area, reconstruct US city

indicators.note: the close of industrial is its final letter

parts.note: to reconstruct something is to do it again, to redo it

explanation.surface: A planning instruction to rebuild an American city near a factory district.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a city in Texas on the Rio Grande, at the Mexican border.

clue.text: Get off! It's not that car that needs towing

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief: you are kidding me

definitions.text: It's not that car that needs towing
definitions.meaning: read literally, a tow truck is told to haul the second car rather than the first

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom, said to someone teasing you, comes from 'pull the other leg', the one with bells on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a scoffing retort to a tall story, and a literal instruction about which vehicle to tow.

clue.text: In film, a rat is caught somehow feeding off other animals

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are caught inside the word for film

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: A movie scene in which a rat gets trapped while scavenging from other creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives on a host and takes its nourishment from it.

clue.text: Fruit and vegetable box reduced by 20 per cent

parts.note: the pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: a five-letter word loses one letter, a fifth of it, from its end

parts.note: a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's offer: a fruit and veg box with a fifth off the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by 20 per cent' removes one letter of five from CHEST, leaving CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural fruit: soft downy stone fruits from a tree grown in warm climates.

clue.text: Romeo embraced by stage heroine who's hard to understand?

indicators.note: the letter for Romeo is held inside the heroine's name

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title heroine of Ibsen's play
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo hugged by a theatrical heroine, someone tricky to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo looks as though he belongs to Juliet, but he is just the radio code letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mixes up words or messages makes them confusing, so such a person is hard to follow.

clue.text: Strange way river is diverted further east

indicators.note: in an across answer east is rightwards, so the river letter shifts along to a later spot

parts.note: a route is a way to go

explanation.surface: A road is rerouted because a river has been diverted eastwards, a strange affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, means unconventional and bizarre, beyond accepted limits.

clue.text: After a brief drink before party, ready to spin yarns

indicators.note: after places the shortened drink behind the a
before places the party ahead of the next piece
brief means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down
a do is a party

indicators.note: to spin round means to turn, so the word for ready reads backwards

parts.note: set means ready, as in 'get set'

explanation.surface: After a quick drink before a party, someone is all set to tell tall tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims NECK to NEC; 'to spin' turns SET into TES. 'Spin yarns' looks like the definition, but only 'yarns' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarns are stories, especially rambling or tall ones; short personal tales told for amusement fit.

clue.text: Flipping tag attached to collar and boater?

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole combination round so it reads from the end

parts.note: a name tag; a name is a label
to collar someone is to grab them

explanation.surface: A straw boater hat with a label fixed to its band, and a collar nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boater' looks like the straw hat but means someone who works a boat; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who works on a canal barge spends his days on a boat, so he is literally a boater.

clue.text: Over in bar, drinkers finally saying cheerio

definitions.meaning: overturned, upside down, with the base pointing upwards

definitions.text: in bar, drinkers finally saying cheerio
definitions.meaning: the toast drinkers give in a pub before draining their glasses

explanation.walkthrough: The toast literally tells drinkers to tip their glasses over until the base points at the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a description of something upended and the familiar drinking salute.

clue.text: Contact former spouse time after time

indicators.note: after places the second time behind the former spouse

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
T again, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps getting in touch with their ex again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone by phone message is to send them a written message, a verb sense.

clue.text: First parts of this old Gershwin number in concert

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the next three words is taken

parts.note: something that numbs; ether was an early anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A request for the opening bars of a vintage Gershwin song played at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a song but is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting jointly, all at once with others.

clue.text: Actress slim? Hard to believe

parts.note: to slim is to diet
'that's rich' is said of something absurd or hard to credit

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a certain actress is slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born film actress and singer, star of The Blue Angel.

clue.text: Yank apprehends hard criminal

indicators.note: apprehends means catches or holds, so the hard letter is held inside

parts.note: to yank is to tug
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An American catches a hardened criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian is a crook who uses force, so the word fits a criminal.

clue.text: Old Communist's struggle with movement after unexpectedly big reverses

indicators.note: after says the struggle and movement pieces come behind the reversed size
reverses turns the size label round so it reads backwards

parts.note: OS is outsize, a garment size larger than expected
to vie is to compete or struggle
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A political tale: the struggle and a movement as some big figure unexpectedly backtracks.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of the old Soviet Union, the Communist state, matching the possessive.

clue.text: Rather dry inside quarry

indicators.note: inside puts the dry letters within the word for quarry

parts.note: the quarry of a hunter is its prey
TT means teetotal, i.e. dry, not drinking

explanation.surface: A rather arid stone quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' looks like a stone pit but is the hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb it means fairly or somewhat, as in 'fairly good'.

clue.text: Victory over political party? That's some kind of joke

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the win above the party

parts.note: a victory is a win
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A cynical voter dismisses an election win for a party as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A tease or prank designed to provoke someone is a sort of jest, from 'winding someone up'.

clue.text: Servicemen protecting the Western Isles with energy? Not so

indicators.note: the servicemen surround and guard the following word, which sits inside them

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
IS is the abbreviation for islands or isles
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Troops guarding the Western Isles of Scotland with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb it means in a different way or else, the opposite of being so.

clue.text: Dropping round, keep quiet, fool

indicators.note: dropping means letting a letter fall out of the next word

parts.note: the keep of a castle is its main tower
a round thing is O-shaped
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop going round, keep quiet, and stop playing the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep quiet' reads as one instruction, but 'keep' is the castle tower and 'quiet' is P.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, a nitwit.

clue.text: Job one secured in advance

indicators.note: the numeral for one is secured within the word for job

parts.note: a post is a job
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A job for someone that was secured ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' looks like 'in advance' but is a verb: to put forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a theory or proposal is to advance it as a basis for argument.

clue.text: Noticed shilling put in pocket

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for an old British shilling
in snooker, a ball put in a pocket has been potted

explanation.surface: Someone saw a shilling being slipped into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth twelve pence; 'put in pocket' is snooker, not a trouser pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Having seen something is having spotted it, past tense.

clue.text: Terrible in-house squabbling

indicators.note: squabbling suggests disorder, so the letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: Terrible infighting within an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means shockingly evil or wicked, a stronger synonym for awful.

clue.text: Turned up lacking confidence? Hardly!

indicators.note: turned means the little word up is read the other way round

parts.note: a shy person lacks confidence

explanation.surface: Someone arrived looking timid? Not a bit of it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' makes PU from UP. The whole clue also defines: someone far from lacking confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushy person is overly assertive, the very opposite of timid.

clue.text: Paper featuring clever people in part

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the abbreviation for part

parts.note: arch can mean cunning or knowing, hence clever
men are people

explanation.surface: A newspaper featuring clever people in one section.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is a writing material made from animal skin, and also a type of stiff paper.
